newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania bourse slow, some dealers optimistic.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania bourse slow, some dealers optimistic.

text.p: The Lithuanian bourse saw slow trade on Tuesday with Hermis and Savings bank active and more optimism over the future, dealers said.
"Although trade was quite slow today, demand for shares and turnover showed the first signs of growth," Arvydas Jacikevichius, a broker with Suprema, told Reuters.
Hermis bank dominated the central market, making one third of the total turnover of 297,720 litas, rising by 3.45 percent to 180 litas.

"Investors were increasingly interested in the blue chips of the bourse, like Hermis Bank, Lithuanian Gas and Birzai Dairy, and if today's tendency remains we shall be able to start talking about stabilisation of the market," Jacikevichius said.
He added that he expected no big price declines this week and was expecting more active trade next week.
Savings Bank registered the biggest single deal in bloc trades of 1.157 million litas at a 231.4 litas price. The price for the shares on the central market was 284 litas per share.
"The decision of the board of the stock exchange to strip the restrictions on price fluctutations in bloc trades also activated the trade," Jacikevichius said.
Grazhina Bachiuliene, a broker with Vilfima, said the bourse's low activity may be explained by few foreign investors.
She said she was expecting an international seminar due in Vilnius next week to stimulate interest.
Lithuanian Gas advanced to 2 litas from 1.9 litas on 110,800 litas turnover.
Birzai Dairy remained unchanged at 10.25 litas on 28,218 litas turnover.
